rgument%20functor%20called%20**tensor**%20%24%5Cotimes%20%3A%20%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%20%5Ctimes%20%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%20%5Cto%20%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%24%20which%20is%20associative%20with%20unit%20%241%20%5Cin%20%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20A%20two-argument%20functor%2C%20also%20called%20a%20%5Bbifunctor%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FBifunctor)%2C%20is%20simply%20a%20functor%20from%20a%20%5Bproduct%20category%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FProduct_category)%2C%20i.e.%20where%20objects%20and%20arrows%20are%20pairs.%0A%20%20%20%20The%20monoidal%20product%20is%20a%20generalisation%20of%20the%20%5Btensor%20product%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FTensor_product)%20of%20linear%20maps%20and%20of%20the%20%5BKronecker%20product%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FKronecker_product)%20of%20matrices.%0A%20%20%20%20Without%20loss%20of%20generality%2C%20we%20may%20assume%20that%20the%20objects%20of%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D%24%20form%20a%20**free%20monoid**%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D_0%5E%5Cstar%24%2C%20i.e.%20they%20are%20lists%20of%20elements%20from%20some%20set%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D_0%24%20of%20generating%20objects.%0A%20%20%20%20(If%20you%20want%20to%20be%20technical%2C%20this%20is%20called%20a%20%5Bcoloured%20PRO%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fncatlab.org%2Fnlab%2Fshow%2FPRO).)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Types%20and%20signatures%0A%0A%20%20%20%20What%20we%20call%20a%20**type**%20is%20such%20a%20list%20of%20generating%20objects%2C%20it%20is%20implemented%20by%20%60Ty%60%2C%20a%20subclass%20of%20%60Ob%60%20with%20an%20attribute%20%60inside%3A%20tuple%5BOb%2C%20...%5D%60.%0A%20%20%20%20The%20default%20value%20is%20the%20empty%20tuple%2C%20i.e.%20the%20unit%20of%20the%20monoid.%0A%20%20%20%20The%20method%20%60tensor%60%20returns%20the%20concatenation%20of%20two%20types%2C%20it%20is%20shortened%20to%20%60%40%60.%0A%20%20%20%20We%20can%20check%20that%20this%20indeed%20satisfies%20the%20axioms%20of%20a%20monoid.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A% %20boxes%2C%20but%20now%20boxes%20have%20types%20(i.e.%20lists%20of%20objects)%20as%20domain%20and%20codomain.%0A%20%20%20%20This%20is%20implemented%20by%20the%20class%20%60monoidal.Box%60%2C%20which%20comes%20with%20a%20method%20%60draw%60%20which%20now%20justifies%20its%20name%3A%20a%20%60Box%60%20is%20drawn%20as%20a%20box%20with%20its%20domain%20and%20codomain%20as%20input%20and%20output%20wires.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(monoidal%2C%20x_1%2C%20y_1%2C%20z_1)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20box%20%3D%20monoidal.Box('box'%2C%20x_1%20%40%20x_1%20%40%20x_1%2C%20y_1%20%40%20z_1)%0A%20%20%20%20box%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(box%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Boxes%20with%20the%20empty%20list%20as%20domain%20and%20codomain%20are%20called%20a%20**states**%20and%20**effects**%20respectively.%0A%20%20%20%20A%20**scalar**%20is%20both%20a%20state%20and%20an%20effect.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Free%20monoidal%20categories%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20can%20finally%20get%20to%20our%20definition%20of%20diagrams%3A%20they%20are%20**arrows%20in%20a%20free%20monoidal%20category**.%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20spell%20this%20out.%0A%20%20%20%20We%20have%20a%20category%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BMonCat%7D%24%20with%20monoidal%20categories%20as%20objects%20and%20monoidal%20functors%20as%20arrows%2C%20i.e.%20functors%20which%20respect%20the%20tensor.%0A%20%20%20%20Similarly%2C%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BMonSig%7D%24%20is%20the%20category%20of%20monoidal%20signatures%20and%20homomorphisms%20between%20them.%0A%20%20%20%20And%20again%2C%20we%20have%20a%20forgetful%20functor%20%24U%20%3A%20%5Cmathbf%7BMonCat%7D%20%5Cto%20%5Cmathbf%7BMonSig%7D%24.%0A%20%20%20%20(This%20is%20where%20we%20need%20to%20assume%20our%20monoidal%20categories%20are%20in%20fact%20coloured%20PROs).%0A%20%20%20%20We%20want%20to%20construct%20its%20left-adjoint%2C%20i.e.%20the%20functor%20%24F%20%3A%20%5Cmathbf%7BMonSig%7D%20%5Cto%20%5Cmathbf%7BMonCat%7D%24%20which%20sends%20a%20monoidal%20signature%20%24G%24%20to%20the%20free%20monoidal%20category%20%24%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D_G%24%20with%20a%20natural%20isomorphism%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%5Cmathbf%7BMonCat%7D(%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D_G%2C%20%5Cmathbf%7BD%7D)%20%5Csimeq%20%5Cmathbf%7BMonSig%7D(G%2C%20U_%5Cmathbf%7BD%7D)%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20If%20you%20know%20some%20abstract%20algebra%2C%20then%20you%20know%20the%20brute%20force%20way%20to%20implement%20such%20a%20beast.%0A%20%20%20%20First%2C%20we%20give%20a%20recursive%20definition%20of%20all%20the%20string%20diagrams%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*%20every%20box%20%24f%20%3A%20x%20%5Cto%20y%20%5Cin%20G%24%20is%20also%20a%20diagram%20%24f%20%3A%20x%20%5Cto%20y%20%5Cin%20%5Cmathbf%7BC%7D_G%24%2C%0A%20%20%20%20*%20for%20every%20type%20%24x%20%5Cin%20G_0%5E%5Cstar%24%2C%20the%20**identity**%20%241_x%20%3A%20x%20%5Cto%20x%24%20is%20a%20diagram%20drawn%20as%20a%20bunch%20of%20parallel%20wires%2C%0A%20%20%20%20*%20for%20every%20composable%20pair%20of%20diagrams%20%24f%20%3A%20x%20%5Cto%20y%24%20and%20%24g%20%3A%20y%20%5Cto%20z%24%2C%20their%20**composition**%20%24f%20g%20%3A%20x%20%5Cto%20z%24%20is%20a%20diagram%20drawn%20as%20vertical%20concatenation%2C%0A%20%20%20%20*%20for%20every%20pair%20of%20diagrams%20%24f%20%3A%20x%20%5Cto%20y%24%20and%20%24f'%20%3A%20x'%20%5Cto%20y'%24%2C%20their%20**tensor**%20%24f%20%5Cotimes%20f'%20%3A%20xx'%20%5Cto%20yy'%24%20is%20diagram%20drawn%20as%20horizontal%20juxtaposition.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Next%2C%20we%20realise%20that%20some%20diagrams%20appear%20multiple%20times%2C%20e.g.%20%24f%20(g%20h)%24%20and%20%24(f%20g)%20h%24%2C%20so%20that%20we%20need%20to%20take%20a%20**quotient**%2C%20i.e.%20putting%20two%20formulae%20in%20the%20same%20**equivalence%20class**%20if%20they%20represent%20the%20same%20diagram.%0A%20%20%20%20Again%2C%20this%20equivalence%20relation%20is%20defined%20recursively%3A%20if%20%24f%20%5Csim%20f'%24%20and%20%24g%20%5Csim%20g'%24%20then%20%24(f%20g)%20%5Csim%20(f'%20g')%24%20and%20%24(f%20%5Cotimes%20g)%20%5Csim%20(f'%20%5Cotimes%20g')%24.%0A%20%20%20%20The%20base%20case%20is%20given%20by%20the%20axioms%20of%20monoidal%20categories%2C%20namely%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*%20**associativity**%3A%20%24f%20(g%20h)%20%5Csim%20(f%20g)%20h%24%20and%20%24f%20%5Cotimes%20(f'%20%5Cotimes%20f'')%20%5Csim%20(f%20%5Cotimes%20f')%20%5Cotimes%20f''%24%0A%20%20%20%20*%20**unit**%3A%20%24(1_x%20f)%20%5Csim%20f%20%5Csim%20(f%201_y)%24%20and%20%24(1%20%5Cotimes%20f)%20%5Csim%20f%20%5Csim%20(f%20%5Cotimes%201)%24%0A%20%20%20%20*%20**interchange%3A**%20%24(1_x%20%5Cotimes%201_y)%20%5Csim%201_%7Bxy%7D%24%20and%20%24(f%20g)%20%5Cotimes%20(f'%20g')%20%5Csim%20(f%20%5Cotimes%20f')%20(g%20%5Cotimes%20g')%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Layers%20and%20whiskering%0A%0A%20%20%20%20While%20the%20first%20two%20are%20straightforward%2C%20the%20third%20axiom%20corresponds%20to%20the%20tensor%20being%20a%20bifunctor%3A%20a)%20the%20tensor%20of%20identity%20is%20the%20identity%20of%20tensor%20and%20b)%20the%20tensor%20of%20a%20pair%20of%20compositions%20is%20the%20composition%20of%20a%20pair%20of%20tensors.%0A%20%20%20%20This%20second%20part%20is%20the%20most%20challenging%20to%20implement.%0A%20%20%20%20Indeed%2C%20remember%20how%20we%20got%20the%20associativity%20and%20unit%20of%20sequential%20composition%20to%20hold%20for%20free%20from%20that%20of%20Python%20tuples.%0A%20%20%20%20We%20could%20try%20to%20play%20the%20same%20trick%20for%20the%20associativity%20and%20unit%20of%20parallel%20composition%2C%20but%20the%20interchange%20axiom%20forces%20these%20two%20types%20of%20tuples%20to%20distribute%20over%20one%20another.%0A%20%20%20%20In%20fact%2C%20we%20can%20use%20interchange%20to%20write%20every%20diagram%20in%20**generic%20form**%2C%20i.e.%20as%20a%20composition%20of%20tensors.%0A%20%20%20%20Furthermore%2C%20we%20can%20always%20write%20it%20so%20that%20every%20tensor%20expression%20contains%20exactly%20one%20box%2C%20e.g.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24f%20%5Cotimes%20f'%20%3D%20(f%201_y)%20%5Cotimes%20(1_%7Bx'%7D%20f')%20%3D%20(f%20%5Cotimes%201_%7Bx'%7D)%20(1_y%20%5Cotimes%20f')%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Such%20a%20tensor%20expression%20is%20called%20a%20**layer**.%0A%20%20%20%20DisCoPy%20can%20also%20fuse%20independent%20boxes%20into%20one%20layer%2C%20for%20example%20%24f%20%5Cotimes%20g%24.%0A%20%20%20%20This%20is%20implemented%20by%20%60Layer%60%2C%20a%20subclass%20of%20%60cat.Box%60%20whose%20%60boxes_or_types%60%20attribute%20is%20a%20compact%20tensor%20word%20of%20boxes%20and%20non-empty%20types.%0A%20%20%20%20It%20contains%20at%20least%20one%20box%2C%20drops%20empty%20types%2C%20and%20tensors%20adjacent%20types%20together.%0A%20%20%20%20Its%20%60boxes_and_offsets%60%20lists%20each%20box%20with%20its%20offset%2C%20i.e.%20the%20number%20of%20wires%20on%20its%20left%20once%20the%20boxes%20before%20it%20are%20applied.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(Ty%2C%20box)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20from%20discopy.monoidal%20import%20Layer%0A%0A%20%20%20%20a%2C%20b%2C%20c%20%3D%20map(Ty%2C%20%22abc%22)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20layer%20%3D%20Layer(a%2C%20box%2C%20b)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20a%20%40%20box%20%40%20b%0A%20%20%20%20return%20Layer%2C%20a%2C%20b%2C%20c%2C%20layer%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20We%20can%20tensor%20a%20layer%20by%20a%20type%20on%20its%20left%20or%20right%2C%20this%20is%20called%20**whiskering**.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(Layer%2C%20a%2C%20b%2C%20box%2C%20c%2C%20layer)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20assert%20layer%20%40%20c%20%3D%3D%20Layer(a%2C%20box%2C%20b%20%40%20c)%0A%20%20%20%20assert%20c%20%40%20layer%20%3D%3D%20Layer(c%20%40%20a%2C%20box%2C%20b)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Tensor%20and%20interchange%0A%0A%20%20%20%20We%20can%20finally%20get%20to%20the%20core%20data%20structure%20of%20DisCoPy%3A%20a%20%60Diagram%60%20is%20an%20arrow%20with%20a%20list%20of%20layers%20%60inside%3A%20tuple%5BLayer%2C%20...%5D%60%20and%20a%20method%20%60tensor%60%20for%20parallel%20composition%2C%20again%20shortened%20to%20%60%40%60.%0A%20%20%20%20This%20is%20implemented%20in%20terms%20of%20whiskering%20using%20the%20previous%20formula%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(Layer%2C%20Ty%2C%20monoidal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20from%20discopy.monoidal%20import%20Diagram%0A%20%20%20%20x_2%2C%20y_2%2C%20x_%2C%20y_%20%3D%20(Ty('x')%2C%20Ty('y')%2C%20Ty('x_')%2C%20Ty('y_'))%0A%20%20%20%20f_1%2C%20f__1%20%3D%20(monoidal.Box('f'%2C%20x_2%2C%20y_2)%2C%20monoidal.Box('f_'%2C%20x_%2C%20y_))%0A%20%20%20%20assert%20f_1%20%40%20f__1%20%3D%3D%20f_1%20%40%20x_%20%3E%3E%20y_2%20%40%20f__1%20%3D%3D%20Diagram(inside%3D(Layer(f_1%2C%20x_)%2C%20Layer(y_2%2C%20f__1))%2C%20dom%3Dx_2%20%40%20x_%2C%20cod%3Dy_2%20%40%20y_)%0A%20%20%20%20f_1%20%40%20f__1%0A%20%20%20%20return%20Diagram%2C%20f_1%2C%20f__1%2C%20x_%2C%20x_2%2C%20y_%2C%20y_2%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20In%20fact%2C%20a%20diagram%20can%20be%20written%20more%20compactly%20than%20as%20its%20list%20of%20layers.%0A%20%20%20%20When%20each%20layer%20has%20one%20box%2C%20as%20here%2C%20the%20domain%2C%20the%20list%20of%20its%20boxes%20and%20the%20**offset**%20for%20each%20box%2C%20i.e.%20the%20number%20of%20wires%20to%20its%20left%2C%20characterise%20a%20diagram.%0A%20%20%20%20The%20methods%20%60encode%60%20and%20%60decode%60%20go%20back%20and%20forth%20between%20a%20diagram%20and%20its%20domain%20with%20one%20list%20of%20boxes%20and%20offsets%20per%20layer%2C%20so%20that%20a%20layer%20with%20several%20boxes%20comes%20back%20as%20one.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(Diagram%2C%
